legal.title: Terms and privacy notice
legal.rowSub: How we use and look after your data
legal.intro: Lyra is an app for art schools, run by {owner}. Here we explain the rules for using it and how we handle personal data, under Mexico’s Federal Law on the Protection of Personal Data Held by Private Parties (LFPDPPP). Each school also has its own terms, which you accept in the app when you register.
legal.who.title: What Lyra is
legal.who.body: Schools use Lyra to register their students and teachers, set their classes and schedules, record attendance and receive payment screenshots. Several schools share the app, but each sees only its own people and records.
legal.roles.title: Who is responsible for your data
legal.roles.body:
Your school is responsible for the data of its students, guardians and teachers: it decides what it’s used for, under its terms. {owner} acts as a processor: it stores and processes that data only to provide the service to the school, following its instructions.

{owner} is responsible for the data of the schools’ accounts and their directors (name, email, phone and the platform’s billing).
legal.data.title: What data we handle
legal.data.body:
Identification and contact data: name, email (your sign-in), phone and photo.

The student’s card: birth date (the age is calculated), emergency contacts and, for minors, the people allowed to pick them up, with their name and photo.

Health data: the physical conditions the student or their guardian choose to declare (see below).

What happens at the school: enrollments, attendance, payment screenshots (screenshots or photos), fees, notices, and the acceptance of the terms (who, which version and when).

Technical data: what’s needed to keep you signed in. We use no advertising cookies or trackers.
legal.health.title: Health data (sensitive data)
legal.health.body:
Health conditions are sensitive personal data. They’re stored only with your express consent, which you give by accepting your school’s terms in the app (the guardian gives it for minors), and they serve only so the school knows what to look out for in class and whom to call in an emergency.

Only you (or your guardian), your school’s directors and the teachers of the classes you take, while you take them, see them. The platform’s administrator never sees them; they never pass to another school and never go in an email. You can change or remove them at any time from your card, and every change is recorded.
legal.purposes.title: What we use it for
legal.purposes.body:
To provide the service: register you, show you your classes, record your attendance, receive and review your payments, tell you about schedule and price changes, send you your account and payment emails, and let the school reach your contacts in an emergency.

We don’t sell your data, use it for advertising or build commercial profiles.
legal.sharing.title: Who it’s shared with
legal.sharing.body:
With your school, as explained above. With the providers that run the app, as processors and only for that: Supabase (database, files and sign-in), Render (the site), Resend (emails) and Cloudflare (the site’s address). Their servers may be outside Mexico; we require them to protect the data as described here.

With authorities, only when the law requires it. Never with other schools: what you do at one school, another doesn’t see.
legal.keeping.title: How long we keep it
legal.keeping.body:
While you’re active at the school. If you stop being active, your card and files are kept for 3 months (we write every month in case you want them deleted sooner), then they’re deleted on their own.

When they’re deleted, your card, photos, contacts, health conditions, authorized people and payment screenshots go. Attendance and payment records stay without your name, so the school’s counts stay right. If you no longer belong to any school, your account is deleted too.
legal.rights.title: Your rights (ARCO) and your consent
legal.rights.body:
You can access your data, correct it, cancel it or object to its use, and withdraw your consent. In the app: your card shows what we store and you edit it whenever you like; in Account › “I want my data deleted” you ask for deletion and confirm it with the link we send you.

You can also ask your school or write to us at {email}, giving your name, your school and what you’re asking for. We answer within 20 business days at most. Withdrawing consent for health data means removing it from your card.
legal.minors.title: Minors
legal.minors.body: Minors have no account of their own. Their mother, father or guardian registers them, fills in their card, accepts the terms and gives the consents for them, and receives their notices. Whoever registers people allowed to pick a minor up declares they have their permission to share their photo. At 18, the school registers the student again with their own account.
legal.security.title: How we protect it
legal.security.body: Connections are encrypted. Every request goes through rules in the database that let each person see only what’s theirs, even if someone tampers with the app. Photos and screenshots are in private storage, reached only through temporary links. Passwords aren’t stored in plain text, and invitation and deletion links expire. If a breach affecting you ever happened, we’d tell you.
legal.use.title: Terms of use
legal.use.body:
Your account is personal: don’t share your password. Use Lyra only for what it’s for: your classes and your children’s. Don’t upload false, someone else’s or illegal content; payment screenshots must be real.

Each school sets its classes, prices, payment methods and its own terms, and answers for them; class payments are made to the school, outside the app. {owner} provides the platform as it is, works to keep it running and may suspend accounts that misuse it. Schools pay {owner} under their agreement.
legal.changes.title: Changes to this notice
legal.changes.body: If we change this text, we publish it here with its date. If the change affects how we use your data, we tell you in the app.
